messages:
devon: heads-up — after the driver bump to 535.86 in us-west-2 at ~03:18 UTC we're seeing SM90 PTX compile failures on a subset of H100 nodes. Affected pods are getting evicted and some Dedicated pools show reduced available capacity. filing a quick thread so we don't lose context.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed: driver-upgrade/535.86 rolled to cluster us-west-2 (cohort=prod-h100) — status: completed — rollout_id=drv-20260318-03.

anya: can you paste the error snippet and an estimate of hosts impacted? rough % capacity? also any correlation with NCCL versions or CUDA runtime?

devon: error snippet from kubelet on one failing node:
```
Mar 18 03:21:12 h100-az1-043 kubelet[...]: containerd: failed to start container: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create device plugin: ptxas fatal   : Unrecoverable error during compilation
ptxas info    : 0 bytes compiled, 0 relocations, 0 bytes of debug info.
Error: cuModuleLoadDataEx() failed: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX
```
kubectl top nodes shows ~9 nodes with consistent GPU evictions; scheduler indicates ~12% capacity loss in prod-h100 pools (roughly 65/540 GPUs offline for serving).

samir: ugh. that matches an SM90 codegen path that changed in the new driver. previous stable was 535.54 for us-west. can we do a targeted rollback to that driver for the h100 cohort and hold the rest? recommend canary rollback to 50 hosts then ramp. also check linked host-level nvcc/cuda-toolkit compatibility — if CUDA runtime is older it can expose PTXAS mismatches.

ops-oncall: opening incident INFRA-2310 and pinging Dedicated-SREs + account-sre for impacted customers. notify: support/escalations on standby.

devon: plan proposal:
1) pause further driver rollouts in all regions (paused via rollout service).
2) rollback daemonset for cohort prod-h100 in us-west-2 to 535.54 (canary=100 hosts)
3) watch eviction rate + API latencies for 15m, if stable ramp to full cohort rollback.
Commands I'll run in order:
```bash
# pause global rollout
rolloutctl set pause driver-upgrade --all
# set driver version on daemonset for us-west-2 h100 cohort
kubectl -n gpu-system set env daemonset/gpu-driver DRIVER_VERSION=535.54 --selector=redwood.cohort=prod-h100 --record
```
Any objections?

anya: +1 to pause. also can we snapshot the failing nodes' /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and collect nvcc --version + nvidia-smi -q output for postmortem? we should capture a failing kernel blob if possible.

infra-bot: monitoring: h100-evictions(us-west-2) spike -> 12% at 03:22 UTC, current -> 11.7%. API p95 token latency (prod) bumped 18% in the last 5m. Alert: INFRA-H100-PTX-1 triggered.

samir: note: NCCL 2.18.x and CUDA 12.3 are expected for this stack. if any nodes are still pinned to an older CUDA runtime (12.1), PTX-to-SASS JIT paths can fail once driver enforces newer assembler semantics. capture /usr/local/cuda/version.txt from the nodes.

devon: executing rollback now. I'll post progress updates. tagging @ops-oncall @anya @samir. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: INFRA-2310 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2310 — please add logs and timeline. escalations page updated in incident doc.

devon: rollback started at 03:38 UTC against 100 canary hosts. initial health checks: 70/100 back to healthy within 90s on the canary. continuing to monitor before full cohort. will update in 10m.
